title: Crisis Management & PR
completion_message: ¡Excelente! La Gestión de Crisis y las Relaciones Públicas son áreas de máxima tensión. Manejar vocabulario como 'damage control', 'mitigate' y 'product recall' te capacita para liderar comunicaciones en los momentos más difíciles de una empresa.

parts.visual:
Términos Clave de Crisis: 
- Damage control (Control de daños / Medidas para minimizar el impacto negativo). 
Ej: The PR team went into damage control after the scandal. 
- Backlash (Reacción negativa violenta del público o clientes). 
Ej: They faced severe backlash over their new pricing policy. 
- Mitigate (Mitigar / Reducir la gravedad de algo). 
Ej: We must take immediate steps to mitigate the risks.
parts.audio: Key Crisis Terms. 'Damage control' refers to measures taken to offset or minimize damage to reputation or operations. For example: The P R team went into damage control after the scandal. 'Backlash' is a strong negative reaction by a large number of people. For example: They faced severe backlash over their new pricing policy. To 'Mitigate' means to make something less severe or painful. For example: We must take immediate steps to mitigate the risks.

parts.visual:
Relaciones Públicas y Acciones: 
- Product recall (Retirada de un producto del mercado por defectos). 
Ej: The car manufacturer issued a massive product recall. 
- Transparency (Transparencia / Honestidad y apertura en la información). 
Ej: In a crisis, transparency is the best policy. 
- Scapegoat (Chivo expiatorio / Persona a la que se culpa por los errores de otros). 
Ej: The marketing manager became the scapegoat for the failed launch.
parts.audio: Public Relations and Actions. A 'Product recall' is a request to return a product after the discovery of safety issues or product defects. For example: The car manufacturer issued a massive product recall. 'Transparency' implies operating in such a way that it is easy for others to see what actions are performed. For example: In a crisis, transparency is the best policy. A 'Scapegoat' is a person who is blamed for the wrongdoings, mistakes, or faults of others. For example: The marketing manager became the scapegoat for the failed launch.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término de Crisis o PR correcto.

questions.question: After the CEO's controversial tweet, the PR department had to do some serious ____. (Control de daños).
The company faced a massive public ____ when they announced the layoffs. (Reacción negativa).
questions.explanation: Backlash = reacción negativa y fuerte del público.

questions.question: We need to find ways to ____ the impact of the supply chain disruption. (Mitigar / Reducir).
questions.explanation: Mitigate = mitigar, reducir el daño o impacto.

questions.question: Due to a faulty battery, the electronics company issued a worldwide product ____. (Retirada del mercado).
questions.explanation: Product recall = retirada de un producto del mercado por defectos.

questions.question: The public demands complete ____ regarding how the data was leaked. (Transparencia).
Instead of taking responsibility, the board used the CFO as a ____. (Chivo expiatorio).
A statement made to the media to clarify a situation is a press ____. (Comunicado de prensa).
A professional whose job is to represent an organization and speak to the media is a ____. (Portavoz).
To repair their public image, the company hired a top-tier ____ firm. (Relaciones Públicas).
The company's reputation was severely ____ by the scandal. (Manchada / Dañada).
questions.explanation: To tarnish a reputation = manchar o dañar la reputación.

questions.question: When a situation gets worse quickly, we say it has ____. (Escalado / Empeorado).
A sudden, unpredictable event that threatens the organization is a ____. (Crisis).
The company had to ____ the rumors that they were going bankrupt. (Desmentir / Negar).
We need to prepare a contingency ____ in case the primary servers fail. (Plan de contingencia).
questions.explanation: Contingency plan = plan de contingencia (Plan B).

questions.question: To express deep regret for a mistake publicly is to issue an ____. (Disculpa).
questions.explanation: Issue an apology = emitir una disculpa formal.

questions.question: An attempt to hide a mistake or illegal activity is a ____. (Encubrimiento).
A person who exposes any kind of information or activity that is deemed illegal or unethical within an organization is a ____. (Denunciante interno).
To limit the spread of negative information, PR teams often engage in ____ control. (Control de rumores/narrativa).
questions.explanation: Spin (o spin control) = manipular la narrativa o información para dar un sesgo favorable.

questions.question: When public trust in a brand is lost, it is very difficult to ____ it. (Recuperar / Restaurar).
The crisis was handled poorly due to a lack of ____ at the executive level. (Previsión).
